questions.question: Explain the important precautions and contraindications to be considered while performing inverted Asanas. / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the important precautions and contraindications to be considered while performing inverted Asanas. [A] / [CO6]
  • • Learn inverted Asanas under the guidance of a qualified Yoga instructor, particularly as a beginner.
  • • Warm up properly and enter and leave the posture slowly; avoid jerky movements.
  • • Do not force the neck or place excessive pressure on the head and cervical spine.
  • • People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma or other serious eye conditions, significant neck/spinal problems,
  • or certain heart conditions should avoid some inversions unless medically cleared.
  • • During pregnancy, or after an injury or surgery, obtain individual clinical advice before attempting inversions.
  • • Stop immediately if pain, dizziness, breathlessness, visual disturbance or unusual discomfort occurs.
  • • Use suitable support and a non-slip surface; avoid practice when exhausted.
  • • Avoid competing with others or holding the posture longer than comfortable.

questions.question: Develop a short Yoga-based programme that combines suitable Asanas and Pranayama for reducing stress and promoting relaxation. / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Develop a short Yoga-based programme that combines suitable Asanas and Pranayama for reducing stress and promoting
  • relaxation. [C] / [CO6]
  • • Begin in a quiet place with comfortable sitting and natural breathing for 2 minutes.
  • • Do gentle neck and shoulder movements for about 2 minutes, without forcing the joints.
  • • Practise Tadasana for 1 minute, followed by gentle cat-cow movements for 2 minutes.
  • • Practise Balasana for about 2 minutes and a comfortable seated forward bend if appropriate.
  • • Perform slow diaphragmatic breathing or gentle alternate-nostril breathing for 3–4 minutes; do not force the breath or hold
  • it.

questions.question: A beginner is learning Pranayama for the first time. Explain the basic principles that should be followed for safe and effective practice. / [CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• A beginner is learning Pranayama for the first time. Explain the basic principles that should be followed for safe and
  • effective practice. [A] / [CO6]
  • • Learn from a qualified instructor and begin with simple breathing techniques.
  • • Choose a clean, quiet and well-ventilated place; sit comfortably with the spine naturally upright.
  • • Start with natural, slow and smooth breathing without straining.
  • • Do not force inhalation or exhalation, over-breathe or hold the breath as a beginner.
  • • Start with a short duration and increase gradually as comfort and control improve.
  • • Practise when comfortable, preferably not immediately after a heavy meal.
  • • Stop if dizziness, tingling, chest discomfort, anxiety or unusual breathlessness occurs and return to normal breathing.
  • • People with significant heart or respiratory conditions should seek clinical advice before starting.
  • • Regularity and comfort are more important than forceful or prolonged practice.
